subject: Re: Dedicated pool timing, OEM ETA, and cloud fallback coordination
messages:
From: Leo Martin <leo@tritonlabs.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool buy window & OEM ETAs

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Triton Labs is excited about Redwood Dedicated for our inference-heavy workloads. Were building the procurement calendar now and want to align on two things:

1) A realistic committed pool delivery window if we sign a 12-month reserved capacity agreement (target: start-of-Q4 availability).
2) OEM / GPU SKU ETAs youve been seeing (we need rough lead times to lock internal approvals).

Attached is a short spreadsheet with our projected steady-state token throughput and an example ramp profile (triton_procurement_requirements.xlsx). Can you please:
- Confirm whether Redwood can reasonably guarantee start-of-Q4 on a Reserved pool for the SKU mix listed, or what the realistic median ETA is;
- Share any vendor/OEM quote contacts or a playbook for aligning hardware lead times vs. cloud backstop options.

Wed like to finalize a mutual action plan by mid-July so our procurement team can queue the PO onto the vendor timeline.

Cheers,
Leo
Senior Platform Engineer
Triton Labs

--
Attachment: triton_procurement_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 84KB)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Leo Martin <leo@tritonlabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool buy window & OEM ETAs

Hi Leo — thanks for the clear deck and numbers.

High level: we can support a start-of-Q4 target, but with two caveats — OEM lead times for specific SKUs can shift the delivery, and we strongly recommend a staged handoff that pairs an initial Reserved pool (capacity anchor) with a cloud fallback window while the OEM queue clears.

Action items I propose:
- Ben (sales) will lead commercial cadence and PO timing.
- Karthik (capacity/product) will request firm OEM quotes for the SKU mix and provide an engineering tolerance matrix (latency and throughput tradeoffs if SKU substitution is required).
- Ill draft a short mutual action plan (MAP) that captures the commit window, acceptance criteria, fallback cloud commit, and billing start.

Two quick asks for you so the MAP is actionable:
1) Confirm your preferred PO date window (earliest/latest you can sign).
2) Confirm whether Triton has any hard SKU constraints (e.g., must be A100-class vs. Ampere-lite is acceptable).

Im attaching a first-pass MAP for review — its intentionally minimal so we can iterate quickly.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Manager, Solutions 
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: MAP-Triton-v1.pdf (one-page MAP, 12KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: NebulaCorp Sales <sales@nebulacorp.com>, Anita Shah <anita.shah@nebulacorp.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Request: firm ETA & SKU-level lead times for Triton Labs deal (DL-2026-1789)

Hi Anita / Nebula team,

Looping you in on a prospective reserved pool (Triton Labs) were trying to align calendar for. Attached is the Triton throughput profile and a short MAP were iterating on. Can you provide:
- SKU-specific lead times (median + 90th percentile) for the next 3 quarters;
- Any block reservation windows you require to hold a manufacturing slot;
- Preliminary per-SKU pricing and minimum purchase quantities.

Context: Triton is targeting an activation date in early October. We will propose a staged acceptance (initial anchor delivered in October, full tranche by December) if OEM queues require it. If you have conservative/backfill cloud options youd recommend, include those so we can fold them into fallback language.

Appreciate a response today or tomorrow if possible; this will inform Tritons PO window.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Principal, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: triton_procurement_requirements.xlsx (referenced)

From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@nebulacorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Leo Martin <leo@tritonlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: firm ETA & SKU-level lead times for Triton Labs deal (DL-2026-1789)

Karthik — thanks for the note and the helpful forecast. Quick summary of what we can commit to today: 

- SKU lead times: A100-equivalent: median 16 weeks, 90th percentile 22 weeks; Ampere-lite (non-premium) : median 10 weeks, 90th percentile 14 weeks.
- Block reservations: we can reserve a tranche with a 30% deposit to secure a Q4 manufacturing window; lead-time clock starts at deposit receipt.
- Pricing: attached is a preliminary quote; final pricing tied to confirmed tranche sizes and delivery schedule (nebulacorp-prelim-quote-20260630.pdf).

Notes and recommendations:
- For your October anchor, Ampere-lite units are the realistic route to hit the window if deposit is received by 7/10.
- If Triton requires strictly A100-class hardware, the earliest conservative delivery starts mid-November with completion into December (give-or-take port/logistics risk).
- We can provide a limited cloud-burst backstop (partner credits) for a one-quarter horizon; well detail that in the final SOW.

Next steps wed suggest:
1) Triton confirm PO deposit window so we can lock a slot.
2) Redwood proposes MAP finalize language around acceptance criteria/fallback and we triage pricing to match tranche sizes.

Happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

Best,
Anita Shah
Director, Strategic Accounts
NebulaCorp

--
Attachment: nebulacorp-prelim-quote-20260630.pdf (quote PDF, 48KB)
